'''Susanna Maria Zimmermann''' (born 1987) is a Swiss mathematician and a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Basel]]. Her research focuses on [[algebraic geometry]], and especially [[Cremona group]]s in [[birational geometry]].

==Education and career==
Zimmermann is from [[Glarus Süd]];{{r|diss}} she was born in 1987.{{r|idref}} In 2004–2005 she studied as [[Rotary Youth Exchange]] student in [[Mumbai]].{{r|cnrs}} She describes herself after finishing high school as "interested in everything";{{r|ups}} inspired by [[Simon Singh]]'s book ''[[Fermat's Last Theorem (book)|Fermat's Last Theorem]]'',{{r|cnrs}} she chose mathematics for its difficulty, originally intending to work in finance. Changing direction after becoming interested in research through meeting other young researchers at her university,{{r|ups}} she defended her Ph.D. in 2016 at the University of Basel. Her dissertation, ''Compositions and relations in the Cremona groups'', was supervised by Jérémy Blanc.{{r|diss|mg}}

In 2016 and 2017 she was a postdoctoral researcher with Stéphane Lamy at [[Toulouse III - Paul Sabatier University]] in France, funded by the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]]. She remained in France as a [[maître de conférences]] (the French equivalent of an associate professor) at the [[University of Angers]] from 2017 to 2022, affiliated there with the Laboratoire Angevin de REcherche en MAthématiques (LAREMA), and completed a [[habilitation]] in 2021.{{r|cv}}

She took a full professorship in 2022 at [[Paris-Saclay University]], in the Mathematical Institute of Orsay.{{r|cv}} In 2025 she took a leave from her position at Paris-Saclay University and returned to the University of Basel as a full professor.{{r|cv|basel}}

She has also served as an ambassador for the Maison Poincaré, a mathematics museum in the [[Institut Henri Poincaré]].{{r|ups}}

==Recognition==
Zimmermann was a 2020 recipient of the [[CNRS Bronze Medal]],{{r|cnrs}} and was named as a junior member of the [[Institut Universitaire de France]] in 2022.{{r|ups}} Her work with Jérémy Blanc and Stéphane Lamy on quotients of higher-dimensional Cremona groups received a 2024 Frontiers of Science Award at the International Congress of Basic Science in Beijing.{{r|frontiers}}

She is a speaker at the 2026 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]].{{r|icm}}
